what_this_is: Reported harvest outcomes. This is the ground truth side of the loop: remote sensing predicts everywhere, reported fields calibrate, and the correction learned from the fields that report is applied to the regions that never will.
why_it_matters: There will never be harvest reports from every growing region on earth. There does not need to be. The residual between what remote sensing said and what a field actually did is one multiplier per crop, and a multiplier can be learned from a handful of honest reports. What it cannot be learned from is nothing.
how_a_report_is_used: scripts/refresh/ledger.py joins each report to every prediction made BEFORE the harvest date, so the error is always measured against a forecast that could not have seen the answer. The result is published in model-scorecard.json, including the count of reports behind it, so a correction resting on two fields is never mistaken for a calibration.

what_a_report_needs.crop: the market class, exactly as the site names it — PINTO, GARBANZO (KABULI), PEA YELLOW
what_a_report_needs.region: one of ne-panhandle, sw-nebraska, ne-colorado, western-colorado, se-wyoming, big-horn, nw-kansas
what_a_report_needs.crop_year: the harvest year, as a number
what_a_report_needs.lb_ac: clean yield in pounds per acre, per harvested acre
what_a_report_needs.harvested_on: YYYY-MM-DD, the date it came off
what_a_report_needs.reported_by: who said so — a name or an operation. A report with no attribution is not evidence.
what_a_report_needs.irrigated: true, false, or null if unknown — this is the single most useful field after the yield itself, because the model cannot see irrigation and the error almost certainly differs between watered and dryland ground
what_a_report_needs.acres: optional, so a quarter section is not weighted the same as a whole farm
what_a_report_needs.note: optional — hail, disease, replant, anything that explains an outlier

standard_of_evidence: A reported yield is OBSERVED evidence and outranks every model on this site. It is never adjusted to fit a prediction. If a report and the model disagree, the model is what is wrong.
